$comment: Shared, committed Claude Code config so every checkout gets the same safety posture and pre-approved permissions. Machine-specific overrides go in the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json. deny takes precedence over allow, so these blocks hold even under --dangerously-skip-permissions (used by ops/gentriduck-devmode.sh on the native Linux automation host). The 'git push ... main' deny rules are DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH only (ADR-0011): they match 'main' as a ref token (not the substring, so 'domain'/'maintenance' branch names are safe), but exotic forms like 'git push origin HEAD' on a checked-out main, or '--mirror', are NOT caught. main's real protection is the denied gh pr merge + the PM being instructed to only ever touch develop; full enforcement needs a separate PM identity (ADR-0011 Alternative D); a server-side ruleset is now live (SEC-1, #190, resolved 2026-07-11 by the maintainer's own repo-settings action -- ruleset 18802582 'Protect main' requires a PR with zero bypass actors and blocks force-push/deletion, ruleset 18802593 blocks force-push/deletion on develop) -- this file's deny-list is now true defence-in-depth, not the primary backstop. SEC-2 (#191): the allow-list used to include a blanket 'Bash(gh *)', which let 'gh api repos/.../pulls/N/merge -X PUT' bypass the 'gh pr merge' deny, and 'gh api .../git/refs/heads/main -X PATCH' bypass the push-to-main denies (deny patterns match the Bash command string, not what it executes) -- 'gh api' is now dropped from the allow-list entirely (no committed script needs it; falls back to a permission prompt if ever required). Accepted residual risk (SEC-2): deny/allow patterns match the literal command string, so 'python3 -c "...gh api..."' or 'xargs gh api' indirection can still slip past both the gh-subcommand allow-list and the deny-list -- this is why SEC-1's server-side ruleset on main/develop (#190, now live) is the real backstop, not this file. 'rm *'/'curl *'/'wget *' stay broadly allowed because the ingestion pipeline (ingestion/*.py) legitimately downloads and cleans up scratch files; scoping those tighter is out of SEC-2's scope. ADR-0022 (#214, 2026-07-11): the blanket 'Bash(gh api*)' deny above is replaced by an enumerated 'gh api repos/*' + '/repos/*' deny (keeps both original SEC-2 REST bypass vectors closed: '.../pulls/N/merge', '.../git/refs/heads/main') plus explicit GraphQL write-mutation denies ('mergePullRequest', 'createCommitOnBranch', 'mergeBranch', '*Ref*', 'enablePullRequestAutoMerge') so those powers stay closed through GraphQL too. 'Bash(gh api graphql*)' is added back to allow, scoped to unblock exactly CV-3's Discussions fetch_open_ideas()/post_triage_comment() (#188/#214). Enumeration is inherently incompletable (a future/missed GraphQL write mutation would be permitted) -- accepted trade-off per the maintainer's choice of the scoped-exception option over a separate low-priv credential; see the ADR for full residual-risk detail, including that string-matching evasion is inherited from SEC-2 and that SEC-1's server-side ruleset (#190, now live -- ruleset 18802582) remains the real backstop for main.
